subject: Verizon 5G Small Cell Infrastructure Applications
overview: The committee approved 22 site-specific applications for 5G wireless infrastructure while adopting a set of 12 standard conditions to address public concerns regarding aesthetics, noise, and neighbor notification. One location was tabled for further review following intense neighborhood opposition and a resident petition.

items.title: Hearing Procedures and Purview
items.summary: Chair McGivern opened the meeting by clarifying that the committee operates under a narrow purview mandated by federal law, which prohibits the denial of wireless applications based on health effects.

items.title: Adoption of Standard Conditions
items.summary: The committee adopted 12 standard conditions for all installations, including 30-day prior notification to neighbors within 100 feet and a requirement that work be completed within 12 months of approval.

items.title: Routine Small Cell Site Approvals
items.summary: Approved 17 routine site applications at various locations including Wareham Street, Higgins Avenue, Killscythe Road, Dexter Street, Albion Street, Winchester Street, New Bern Avenue, Alfred Street, Harvard Street, Princeton Street, Marion Street, George Street, Mystic Avenue, Winthrop Street, and Boston Avenue.

items.title: Motion for Moratorium and Public Comment
items.summary: The committee denied a request by Councilor Michael Marks to delay all approvals until the city could update its policy, citing the risk of legal action by Verizon for missing federal shot clock deadlines.

items.title: 48 Granville Avenue
items.summary: Approved the application with a specific condition that the existing streetlight must remain on the pole, addressing concerns raised by resident Charlene Roy.

items.title: 4 Colby Street
items.summary: Approved the installation on Colby Street despite health and safety concerns raised by Joseph Nazaro regarding proximity to Tufts University playing fields.

items.title: 333 Main Street
items.summary: Approved the application following discussion with Luke Preisner and Council President Caraviello regarding the line of sight for third-floor residents.

items.title: 600 Boston Avenue
items.summary: Approved the location near St. Clement Elementary School with a condition to confirm that the final pole height meets the proposed clearance standards.

items.title: 549 Main Street
items.summary: Approved the application with an added condition that the equipment must not obstruct vehicular movements at the intersection with Ellesmere Terrace.

items.title: 101 Sheridan Avenue
items.summary: Tabled the application to allow Verizon to explore alternative locations after residents submitted a 34-signature petition against the installation in their neighborhood.

items.title: Continuance of Public Hearing
items.summary: The committee voted to continue the public hearing for the remaining 20 applications to Wednesday, April 14, 2021, at 7:00 PM.
